questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Tight multi-agency July 7 convergence on a NE-Taiwan / Zhe-Min-to-Zhejiang track further strengthens Zhejiang's lead for largest evacuation total by July 11. Taiwan CWA Director Lu Guo-chen and forecaster Huang En-hong reported July 7 that international NWP/AI models have largely converged with low expected track shift, favoring a 'Northwest Typhoon' path past Keelung/NE Taiwan sea (citing 2019 Lekima/Wenling and 2007 Wipha/Cangnan analogs; CNA/NOWnews). CMA Chief Typhoon Forecaster Xiang Chunyi expects Bavi (Cat 4-5, 58-62 m/s, 1000+ km diameter, gale radius expanding to 400-500 km) to brush northern Taiwan July 11 daytime and make landfall near the Zhejiang-Fujian border July 11 afternoon-evening, explicitly comparing a direct Zhejiang strike to 2019 Lekima (1.08M evacuated in Zhejiang; NBD/CCTV), while Bloomberg/Hindustan Times cites NMC expecting Zhejiang landfall Saturday afternoon/evening, Shanghai Met highlights south-central Zhejiang to northern Fujian (secondary northern Zhejiang/northward) late July 11, and KMA tracks north along China's eastern coast. Because July 11 afternoon-evening landfall places peak preemptive evacuations right before the July 11 cutoff, and Bavi's 400-500 km gale radius puts populous, Meiyu-saturated Wenzhou/Taizhou/Ningbo/Zhoushan squarely in the dangerous right-front quadrant even on a northern Fujian (Fuding/Ningde) landfall, Zhejiang rises +0.075 (0.605 -> 0.680). Fujian trims slightly (0.270 -> 0.250) retaining strong probability if Bavi makes northern Taiwan landfall or tracks WNW into Fuzhou/Ningde. Far-north and far-south tails compress: Shanghai 0.065 -> 0.045 (later July 11-12 timing), Jiangsu 0.025 -> 0.015, Guangdong 0.025 -> 0.005 (0.005 residual).

questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Tight multi-agency model convergence on July 7 narrows the mainland landfall corridor sharply onto Zhejiang and northern Fujian while collapsing far-south Guangdong risk. Taiwan CWA stated July 7 that international models have converged on passing offshore NE/north of Taiwan ('Northwest Typhoon' near Keelung Islet, citing 2019 Lekima/Zhejiang, 2007 Wipha/Zhejiang, 2004 Aere/Fujian, and secondary NE-Taiwan landfall like 2012 Saola/Fujian; CNA/NOWnews). CMA Chief Forecaster Xiang Chunyi forecast July 7 that Bavi will most likely brush northern Taiwan July 11 and land near the Zhejiang-Fujian border July 11 afternoon-evening (secondary scenario: land northern Taiwan then Zhe-Min coast; NBD/CNA), while Shanghai Met targets south-central Zhejiang to northern Fujian (secondary: northern Zhejiang or moving north offshore), Bloomberg/HT reports NMC expecting Zhejiang landfall Saturday, and KMA leans north along China's eastern coast. Updating our 5-regime model conditional on qualifying mainland landfall (P_landfall ~88%): Zhejiang climbs +0.070 (0.460 -> 0.530) capturing both south-central Zhejiang (Cangnan/Wenzhou/Taizhou) and direct northern Zhejiang scenarios; Fujian remains a strong #2 at 0.395 (-0.020 from 0.415) because NW tracks from Keelung (~25.2N) directly intersect northern Fujian (Fuding/Xiapu/Ningde) and secondary northern-Taiwan landfalls overwhelmingly strike Fujian (~78%) with higher mainland-landfall conditioning than offshore-recurve Zhejiang tracks. Tails compress: Shanghai 0.050 -> 0.040, Jiangsu 0.025 -> 0.015, Guangdong 0.040 -> 0.015 (0.005 residual for Shandong/Liaoning).

local_articles.title: Catastrophic storms to test China's resilience in 2026, scientists warn
local_articles.snippet: SHANGHAI/BEIJING, July 8 - The floodwaters that ravaged southern China this week look set to expand to other provinces with the imminent arrival of Super Typhoon Bavi, with scientists warning extreme weather would only grow more frequent this year. The expected weather systems will be sure to test the resilience of the country's densely populated cities and rural communities. China's National Climate Center expects up to six typhoons to form in the Northwest Pacific and South China Sea in July, more than the average of 3.8. Of these storms, up to three could make landfall, above the norm of 1.8. The intensity of the cyclones will also be stronger, it said. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’. A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique.
